mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises above 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rises and interest rates are high, economic growth slows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the joint effect does not predict negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: Lower federal funds rates stimulate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If low rates do not correlate with positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production indicates economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If production growth does not lead to positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates predict positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If low rates do not predict positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If employment growth does not correlate with positive returns.
